```java
/**
 * Thread safety implications of shallow vs deep copying
 */
public class CopyThreadSafety {
    
    /**
     * Demonstrate thread safety issues with shallow copying
     */
    public static void demonstrateThreadSafetyIssues() throws InterruptedException {
        System.out.println("=== THREAD SAFETY ISSUES WITH SHALLOW COPY ===\n");
        
        Customer sharedCustomer = new Customer("THREAD_001", "Concurrent User", "concurrent@test.com");
        sharedCustomer.setAddress(new Address("123 Shared St", "Concurrent City", "CC", "12345", "USA"));
        
        // Create shallow copies for multiple threads
        Customer shallowCopy1 = new Customer(sharedCustomer);
        Customer shallowCopy2 = new Customer(sharedCustomer);
        
        CountDownLatch latch = new CountDownLatch(2);
        List<String> results = Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList<>());
        
        // Thread 1 modifies address through shallow copy 1
        Thread thread1 = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
                    shallowCopy1.getAddress().setStreet("Thread1 Street " + i);
                    Thread.sleep(1); // Simulate work
                }
                results.add("Thread 1 completed");
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            } finally {
                latch.countDown();
            }
        });
        
        // Thread 2 modifies address through shallow copy 2
        Thread thread2 = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
                    shallowCopy2.getAddress().setStreet("Thread2 Avenue " + i);
                    Thread.sleep(1); // Simulate work
                }
                results.add("Thread 2 completed");
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            } finally {
                latch.countDown();
            }
        });
        
        thread1.start();
        thread2.start();
        latch.await();
        
        System.out.println("Final address state: " + sharedCustomer.getAddress());
        System.out.println("✗ PROBLEM: Race condition caused unpredictable final state");
        System.out.println("✗ Both threads modified the same Address object");
        System.out.println("✗ Data corruption and inconsistent state possible\n");
    }
    
    /**
     * Demonstrate thread safety with deep copying
     */
    public static void demonstrateThreadSafeDeepCopy() throws InterruptedException {
        System.out.println("=== THREAD SAFETY WITH DEEP COPY ===\n");
        
        Customer originalCustomer = new Customer("SAFE_001", "Safe User", "safe@test.com");
        originalCustomer.setAddress(new Address("456 Safe St", "Safe City", "SC", "54321", "USA"));
        
        // Create deep copies for multiple threads
        Customer deepCopy1 = originalCustomer.createDeepCopy();
        Customer deepCopy2 = originalCustomer.createDeepCopy();
        
        CountDownLatch latch = new CountDownLatch(2);
        
        // Thread 1 modifies its own deep copy
        Thread thread1 = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
                    deepCopy1.getAddress().setStreet("Thread1 Independent " + i);
                    Thread.sleep(1); // Simulate work
                }
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            } finally {
                latch.countDown();
            }
        });
        
        // Thread 2 modifies its own deep copy
        Thread thread2 = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
                    deepCopy2.getAddress().setStreet("Thread2 Independent " + i);
                    Thread.sleep(1); // Simulate work
                }
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            } finally {
                latch.countDown();
            }
        });
        
        thread1.start();
        thread2.start();
        latch.await();
        
        System.out.println("Original address: " + originalCustomer.getAddress());
        System.out.println("Deep copy 1 address: " + deepCopy1.getAddress());
        System.out.println("Deep copy 2 address: " + deepCopy2.getAddress());
        System.out.println("✓ SUCCESS: Each thread has independent data");
        System.out.println("✓ No race conditions or data corruption");
        System.out.println("✓ Thread-safe by design\n");
    }
}

/**
 * Best practices for implementing copying strategies
 */
public class CopyBestPractices {
    
    /**
     * Builder pattern for safe object construction and copying
     */
    public static class CustomerBuilder {
        private String customerId;
        private String name;
        private String email;
        private Address address;
        private List<Order> orders = new ArrayList<>();
        private Map<String, String> preferences = new HashMap<>();
        
        public CustomerBuilder customerId(String customerId) {
            this.customerId = customerId;
            return this;
        }
        
        public CustomerBuilder name(String name) {
            this.name = name;
            return this;
        }
        
        public CustomerBuilder email(String email) {
            this.email = email;
            return this;
        }
        
        public CustomerBuilder address(Address address) {
            this.address = address;
            return this;
        }
        
        public CustomerBuilder addOrder(Order order) {
            this.orders.add(order);
            return this;
        }
        
        public CustomerBuilder addPreference(String key, String value) {
            this.preferences.put(key, value);
            return this;
        }
        
        // Build with shallow copy semantics
        public Customer buildShallow() {
            Customer customer = new Customer(customerId, name, email);
            customer.setAddress(address); // Shallow reference
            orders.forEach(customer::addOrder); // Shallow references
            preferences.forEach(customer::setPreference);
            return customer;
        }
        
        // Build with deep copy semantics
        public Customer buildDeep() {
            Customer customer = new Customer(customerId, name, email);
            
            // Deep copy address
            if (address != null) {
                customer.setAddress(new Address(address));
            }
            
            // Deep copy orders
            for (Order order : orders) {
                customer.addOrder(new Order(order));
            }
            
            // Copy preferences (String keys/values are immutable)
            preferences.forEach(customer::setPreference);
            
            return customer;
        }
        
        // Create builder from existing customer (for copying)
        public static CustomerBuilder from(Customer customer) {
            CustomerBuilder builder = new CustomerBuilder()
                .customerId(customer.getCustomerId())
                .name(customer.getName())
                .email(customer.getEmail());
            
            if (customer.getAddress() != null) {
                builder.address(customer.getAddress());
            }
            
            customer.getOrderHistory().forEach(builder::addOrder);
            customer.getPreferences().forEach(builder::addPreference);
            
            return builder;
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy strategy interface for flexible copying approaches
     */
    public interface CopyStrategy<T> {
        T copy(T original);
    }
    
    public static class ShallowCopyStrategy implements CopyStrategy<Customer> {
        @Override
        public Customer copy(Customer original) {
            return new Customer(original);
        }
    }
    
    public static class DeepCopyStrategy implements CopyStrategy<Customer> {
        @Override
        public Customer copy(Customer original) {
            return original.createDeepCopy();
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy context for determining appropriate copy strategy
     */
    public enum CopyContext {
        CACHING,           // Shallow copy often appropriate
        SECURITY_BOUNDARY, // Deep copy required
        THREAD_ISOLATION,  // Deep copy required
        PERFORMANCE_CRITICAL, // Shallow copy preferred
        DATA_MODIFICATION, // Deep copy required
        READ_ONLY_ACCESS   // Shallow copy acceptable
    }
    
    /**
     * Smart copy factory that chooses strategy based on context
     */
    public static class SmartCopyFactory {
        
        public static Customer createCopy(Customer original, CopyContext context) {
            switch (context) {
                case SECURITY_BOUNDARY:
                case THREAD_ISOLATION:
                case DATA_MODIFICATION:
                    return original.createDeepCopy();
                
                case CACHING:
                case PERFORMANCE_CRITICAL:
                case READ_ONLY_ACCESS:
                    return new Customer(original);
                
                default:
                    // Default to safe deep copy
                    return original.createDeepCopy();
            }
        }
        
        public static List<Customer> createCopyList(List<Customer> originalList, CopyContext context) {
            return originalList.stream()
                              .map(customer -> createCopy(customer, context))
                              .collect(Collectors.toList());
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Immutable customer class to eliminate copying concerns
     */
    public static final class ImmutableCustomer {
        private final String customerId;
        private final String name;
        private final String email;
        private final Address address;
        private final List<Order> orderHistory;
        private final Map<String, String> preferences;
        
        public ImmutableCustomer(String customerId, String name, String email,
                               Address address, List<Order> orders, Map<String, String> preferences) {
            this.customerId = customerId;
            this.name = name;
            this.email = email;
            this.address = address != null ? new Address(address) : null;
            this.orderHistory = Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(orders));
            this.preferences = Collections.unmodifiableMap(new HashMap<>(preferences));
        }
        
        // Factory method from mutable customer
        public static ImmutableCustomer from(Customer customer) {
            return new ImmutableCustomer(
                customer.getCustomerId(),
                customer.getName(),
                customer.getEmail(),
                customer.getAddress(),
                customer.getOrderHistory(),
                customer.getPreferences()
            );
        }
        
        // Getters return defensive copies
        public String getCustomerId() { return customerId; }
        public String getName() { return name; }
        public String getEmail() { return email; }
        public Address getAddress() { return address != null ? new Address(address) : null; }
        public List<Order> getOrderHistory() { return orderHistory; } // Already unmodifiable
        public Map<String, String> getPreferences() { return preferences; } // Already unmodifiable
        
        // Builder for creating modified copies
        public ImmutableCustomer withName(String newName) {
            return new ImmutableCustomer(customerId, newName, email, address, 
                                       new ArrayList<>(orderHistory), new HashMap<>(preferences));
        }
        
        public ImmutableCustomer withEmail(String newEmail) {
            return new ImmutableCustomer(customerId, name, newEmail, address,
                                       new ArrayList<>(orderHistory), new HashMap<>(preferences));
        }
    }
}
```

---

### **Decision Matrix: When to Use Each Approach**

| Scenario | Shallow Copy | Deep Copy | Immutable Objects |
|----------|-------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Caching/Performance** | ✅ Preferred | ❌ Too expensive | ✅ Ideal |
| **Security Boundaries** | ❌ Dangerous | ✅ Required | ✅ Ideal |
| **Thread Safety** | ❌ Race conditions | ✅ Safe | ✅ Inherently safe |
| **Data Modification** | ❌ Side effects | ✅ Required | ✅ Copy-on-write |
| **Memory Constrained** | ✅ Efficient | ❌ High overhead | ⚠️ Depends |
| **Read-Only Access** | ✅ Acceptable | ⚠️ Overkill | ✅ Perfect |

### **Interview Follow-Up Questions**

1. **Q**: "How do you implement deep copying for circular references?"
   **A**: Use visited object tracking:
   ```java
   public Customer deepCopy(Set<Object> visited) {
       if (visited.contains(this)) return this; // Handle cycles
       visited.add(this);
       // Perform deep copy with visited set
   }
   ```

2. **Q**: "What's the performance impact of deep copying large object graphs?"
   **A**: 
   - **Time**: O(n) where n is total objects in graph
   - **Space**: 2x memory usage during copying
   - **Mitigation**: Copy-on-write, lazy copying, object pooling

3. **Q**: "How does serialization relate to deep copying?"
   **A**: Serialization provides automatic deep copying:
   ```java
   public Customer deepCopyViaSerialization() throws Exception {
       ByteArrayOutputStream bos = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
       ObjectOutputStream out = new ObjectOutputStream(bos);
       out.writeObject(this);
       
       ByteArrayInputStream bis = new ByteArrayInputStream(bos.toByteArray());
       ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream(bis);
       return (Customer) in.readObject();
   }
   ```

4. **Q**: "When would you choose immutable objects over copying?"
   **A**: Immutable objects eliminate copying concerns:
   - **Thread safety**: No synchronization needed
   - **Caching**: Safe to share references
   - **Security**: Cannot be modified after creation
   - **Functional programming**: Enables pure functions

---

### **Complexity Analysis**

**Time Complexity**:
- **Shallow copy**: O(1) - Only copies references
- **Deep copy**: O(n) - Where n is total objects in object graph
- **Immutable creation**: O(n) - One-time cost, then O(1) sharing

**Space Complexity**:
- **Shallow copy**: O(1) - No additional objects created
- **Deep copy**: O(n) - Duplicates entire object graph
- **Immutable objects**: O(n) - But enables safe sharing

**Performance Characteristics**:
- **Shallow copy**: 10-100x faster than deep copy
- **Deep copy**: 2-10x memory usage during operation
- **Security**: Deep copy prevents 100% of shared mutable state vulnerabilities

---

This comprehensive analysis demonstrates that **shallow vs deep copying is a critical architectural decision** with significant implications for:

- **Security**: Shallow copying can create serious vulnerabilities in enterprise systems
- **Thread safety**: Deep copying provides isolation, shallow copying requires synchronization
- **Performance**: Shallow copying is faster but deep copying prevents bugs
- **Memory management**: Trade-offs between speed and memory usage
- **API design**: Choosing the right copying strategy based on use case context

The key insight is that **the choice between shallow and deep copying should be made consciously based on security, performance, and correctness requirements**, not by default or accident.

**Q35: How do you implement a copy constructor in Java?**

**Question**: Explain how to implement copy constructors in Java comprehensively. What are the different approaches, best practices, and pitfalls? How do copy constructors relate to cloning, serialization, and builder patterns? ### **Brute Force Approach - Basic Understanding**

Most developers know Java lacks native copy constructors but don't understand proper implementation:

```java
// Naive approach - "just copy all fields"
public class Person {
    String name;
    List<String> hobbies;
    
    public Person(Person other) {
        this.name = other.name;
        this.hobbies = other.hobbies; // WRONG - shallow copy!
    }
}

// Developer doesn't understand:
```

**Problems with this approach**:

- Missing inheritance hierarchy handling
- No validation or null checking
- Cannot handle circular references
- No consideration for immutability patterns

### **Optimal Solution - Comprehensive Copy Constructor Mastery**

Understanding copy constructors as a fundamental pattern for safe object creation in enterprise systems:

```java
/**
 * Comprehensive Copy Constructor Demonstration System
 * 
 * This system demonstrates copy constructor implementation through
 * a real-world enterprise document management system where proper
 * copying is critical for version control, collaboration, and data integrity.
 * 
 * Real-world context: Document management systems like SharePoint,
 * Google Workspace, and Confluence where document copying must preserve
 * all metadata, permissions, and content while maintaining data integrity.
 */

// ============================================================================
// BASIC COPY CONSTRUCTOR PATTERNS
// ============================================================================

/**
 * Base document class demonstrating fundamental copy constructor patterns
 */
public class Document {
    protected final String documentId;
    protected String title;
    protected String content;
    protected Date createdDate;
    protected Date lastModified;
    protected String author;
    protected List<String> tags;
    protected Map<String, String> metadata;
    
    // Primary constructor
    public Document(String documentId, String title, String author) {
        this.documentId = validateDocumentId(documentId);
        this.title = validateTitle(title);
        this.author = validateAuthor(author);
        this.createdDate = new Date();
        this.lastModified = new Date();
        this.content = "";
        this.tags = new ArrayList<>();
        this.metadata = new HashMap<>();
    }
    
    /**
     * COPY CONSTRUCTOR - Fundamental Pattern
     * 
     * Key principles:
     * 1. Null checking and validation
     * 2. Deep copying of mutable objects
     * 3. Preserving immutable references
     * 4. Maintaining object invariants
     */
    public Document(Document other) {
        // Null check - critical for robustness
        if (other == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source document cannot be null");
        }
        
        // Copy immutable fields directly (String, primitives)
        this.documentId = other.documentId; // String is immutable
        this.title = other.title;           // String is immutable
        this.author = other.author;         // String is immutable
        
        // Deep copy mutable objects
        this.createdDate = other.createdDate != null ? 
            new Date(other.createdDate.getTime()) : null;
        this.lastModified = other.lastModified != null ? 
            new Date(other.lastModified.getTime()) : null;
        
        // Deep copy content (String is immutable, but could be null)
        this.content = other.content;
        
        // Deep copy collections
        this.tags = other.tags != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.tags) : new ArrayList<>();
        this.metadata = other.metadata != null ? 
            new HashMap<>(other.metadata) : new HashMap<>();
        
        // Validate copied state
        validateCopiedState();
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor with modification - Builder-like pattern
     */
    public Document(Document other, String newTitle) {
        this(other); // Call primary copy constructor
        this.title = validateTitle(newTitle);
        this.lastModified = new Date(); // Update modification time
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor with selective copying
     */
    public Document(Document other, boolean copyMetadata, boolean copyTags) {
        // Copy basic fields
        if (other == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source document cannot be null");
        }
        
        this.documentId = generateNewId(); // Generate new ID for copy
        this.title = other.title + " (Copy)";
        this.author = other.author;
        this.content = other.content;
        this.createdDate = new Date(); // New creation date
        this.lastModified = new Date();
        
        // Selective copying based on parameters
        this.tags = copyTags && other.tags != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.tags) : new ArrayList<>();
        this.metadata = copyMetadata && other.metadata != null ? 
            new HashMap<>(other.metadata) : new HashMap<>();
        
        validateCopiedState();
    }
    
    // Validation methods
    private String validateDocumentId(String id) {
        if (id == null || id.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Document ID cannot be null or empty");
        }
        return id.trim();
    }
    
    private String validateTitle(String title) {
        if (title == null || title.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Document title cannot be null or empty");
        }
        if (title.length() > 255) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Document title cannot exceed 255 characters");
        }
        return title.trim();
    }
    
    private String validateAuthor(String author) {
        if (author == null || author.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Document author cannot be null or empty");
        }
        return author.trim();
    }
    
    private void validateCopiedState() {
        if (documentId == null || title == null || author == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Document copy is in invalid state");
        }
        if (tags == null || metadata == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Collections cannot be null after copying");
        }
    }
    
    private String generateNewId() {
        return "DOC_" + System.currentTimeMillis() + "_" + (int)(Math.random() * 1000);
    }
    
    // Getters and utility methods
    public String getDocumentId() { return documentId; }
    public String getTitle() { return title; }
    public String getContent() { return content; }
    public String getAuthor() { return author; }
    public Date getCreatedDate() { return createdDate != null ? new Date(createdDate.getTime()) : null; }
    public Date getLastModified() { return lastModified != null ? new Date(lastModified.getTime()) : null; }
    public List<String> getTags() { return new ArrayList<>(tags); }
    public Map<String, String> getMetadata() { return new HashMap<>(metadata); }
    
    public void setTitle(String title) { 
        this.title = validateTitle(title);
        this.lastModified = new Date();
    }
    
    public void setContent(String content) { 
        this.content = content;
        this.lastModified = new Date();
    }
    
    public void addTag(String tag) {
        if (tag != null && !tag.trim().isEmpty()) {
            tags.add(tag.trim());
            this.lastModified = new Date();
        }
    }
    
    public void setMetadata(String key, String value) {
        if (key != null && !key.trim().isEmpty()) {
            metadata.put(key.trim(), value);
            this.lastModified = new Date();
        }
    }
    
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return String.format("Document{id='%s', title='%s', author='%s', tags=%d, metadata=%d}", 
            documentId, title, author, tags.size(), metadata.size());
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// INHERITANCE HIERARCHY COPY CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

/**
 * Specialized document with additional fields - demonstrates inheritance copying
 */
public class TechnicalDocument extends Document {
    private String technicalLevel;
    private List<String> prerequisites;
    private Map<String, String> codeExamples;
    private List<String> reviewers;
    private String version;
    
    // Primary constructor
    public TechnicalDocument(String documentId, String title, String author, String technicalLevel) {
        super(documentId, title, author);
        this.technicalLevel = validateTechnicalLevel(technicalLevel);
        this.prerequisites = new ArrayList<>();
        this.codeExamples = new HashMap<>();
        this.reviewers = new ArrayList<>();
        this.version = "1.0";
    }
    
    /**
     * COPY CONSTRUCTOR FOR INHERITANCE
     * 
     * Key principles:
     * 1. Call parent copy constructor first
     * 2. Copy derived class fields
     * 3. Maintain type-specific invariants
     * 4. Handle polymorphic copying
     */
    public TechnicalDocument(TechnicalDocument other) {
        super(other); // Call parent copy constructor
        
        if (other == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source technical document cannot be null");
        }
        
        // Copy derived class fields
        this.technicalLevel = other.technicalLevel;
        this.version = other.version;
        
        // Deep copy derived collections
        this.prerequisites = other.prerequisites != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.prerequisites) : new ArrayList<>();
        this.codeExamples = other.codeExamples != null ? 
            new HashMap<>(other.codeExamples) : new HashMap<>();
        this.reviewers = other.reviewers != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.reviewers) : new ArrayList<>();
        
        validateTechnicalDocumentState();
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor from base class - UPCASTING COPY
     * Creates TechnicalDocument from regular Document
     */
    public TechnicalDocument(Document baseDocument, String technicalLevel) {
        super(baseDocument); // Copy base document data
        
        this.technicalLevel = validateTechnicalLevel(technicalLevel);
        this.prerequisites = new ArrayList<>();
        this.codeExamples = new HashMap<>();
        this.reviewers = new ArrayList<>();
        this.version = "1.0";
        
        validateTechnicalDocumentState();
    }
    
    /**
     * Polymorphic copy constructor - handles both base and derived types
     */
    public static TechnicalDocument createCopy(Document source) {
        if (source == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source document cannot be null");
        }
        
        if (source instanceof TechnicalDocument) {
            // Copy as TechnicalDocument (preserves all data)
            return new TechnicalDocument((TechnicalDocument) source);
        } else {
            // Convert regular Document to TechnicalDocument
            return new TechnicalDocument(source, "BEGINNER");
        }
    }
    
    private String validateTechnicalLevel(String level) {
        if (level == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Technical level cannot be null");
        }
        
        String upperLevel = level.toUpperCase();
        if (!Arrays.asList("BEGINNER", "INTERMEDIATE", "ADVANCED", "EXPERT").contains(upperLevel)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid technical level: " + level);
        }
        
        return upperLevel;
    }
    
    private void validateTechnicalDocumentState() {
        if (technicalLevel == null || version == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Technical document copy is in invalid state");
        }
        if (prerequisites == null || codeExamples == null || reviewers == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Technical document collections cannot be null");
        }
    }
    
    // Technical document specific methods
    public void addPrerequisite(String prerequisite) {
        if (prerequisite != null && !prerequisite.trim().isEmpty()) {
            prerequisites.add(prerequisite.trim());
        }
    }
    
    public void addCodeExample(String language, String code) {
        if (language != null && code != null) {
            codeExamples.put(language.trim(), code);
        }
    }
    
    public void addReviewer(String reviewer) {
        if (reviewer != null && !reviewer.trim().isEmpty()) {
            reviewers.add(reviewer.trim());
        }
    }
    
    // Getters
    public String getTechnicalLevel() { return technicalLevel; }
    public String getVersion() { return version; }
    public List<String> getPrerequisites() { return new ArrayList<>(prerequisites); }
    public Map<String, String> getCodeExamples() { return new HashMap<>(codeExamples); }
    public List<String> getReviewers() { return new ArrayList<>(reviewers); }
    
    public void setVersion(String version) { 
        this.version = version;
    }
    
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return String.format("TechnicalDocument{%s, level='%s', version='%s', prerequisites=%d, examples=%d}", 
            super.toString(), technicalLevel, version, prerequisites.size(), codeExamples.size());
    }
}

/**
 * Collaborative document with real-time editing capabilities
 */
public class CollaborativeDocument extends Document {
    private List<String> collaborators;
    private Map<String, Date> editHistory;
    private boolean isLocked;
    private String lockOwner;
    private List<String> comments;
    
    public CollaborativeDocument(String documentId, String title, String author) {
        super(documentId, title, author);
        this.collaborators = new ArrayList<>();
        this.editHistory = new HashMap<>();
        this.isLocked = false;
        this.lockOwner = null;
        this.comments = new ArrayList<>();
        
        // Add creator as first collaborator
        this.collaborators.add(author);
        this.editHistory.put(author, new Date());
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor for collaborative document
     */
    public CollaborativeDocument(CollaborativeDocument other) {
        super(other);
        
        if (other == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source collaborative document cannot be null");
        }
        
        // Deep copy collaborative fields
        this.collaborators = other.collaborators != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.collaborators) : new ArrayList<>();
        
        // Deep copy edit history (Date objects are mutable!)
        this.editHistory = new HashMap<>();
        if (other.editHistory != null) {
            for (Map.Entry<String, Date> entry : other.editHistory.entrySet()) {
                this.editHistory.put(entry.getKey(), 
                    entry.getValue() != null ? new Date(entry.getValue().getTime()) : null);
            }
        }
        
        this.isLocked = other.isLocked;
        this.lockOwner = other.lockOwner;
        this.comments = other.comments != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.comments) : new ArrayList<>();
        
        validateCollaborativeState();
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor with collaboration reset
     */
    public CollaborativeDocument(CollaborativeDocument other, String newOwner, boolean resetCollaboration) {
        super(other);
        
        if (resetCollaboration) {
            // Reset collaboration state for new document
            this.collaborators = new ArrayList<>();
            this.collaborators.add(newOwner);
            this.editHistory = new HashMap<>();
            this.editHistory.put(newOwner, new Date());
            this.isLocked = false;
            this.lockOwner = null;
            this.comments = new ArrayList<>();
        } else {
            // Preserve collaboration state
            this.collaborators = other.collaborators != null ? 
                new ArrayList<>(other.collaborators) : new ArrayList<>();
            this.editHistory = new HashMap<>();
            if (other.editHistory != null) {
                for (Map.Entry<String, Date> entry : other.editHistory.entrySet()) {
                    this.editHistory.put(entry.getKey(), 
                        entry.getValue() != null ? new Date(entry.getValue().getTime()) : null);
                }
            }
            this.isLocked = other.isLocked;
            this.lockOwner = other.lockOwner;
            this.comments = other.comments != null ? 
                new ArrayList<>(other.comments) : new ArrayList<>();
        }
        
        validateCollaborativeState();
    }
    
    private void validateCollaborativeState() {
        if (collaborators == null || editHistory == null || comments == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Collaborative document collections cannot be null");
        }
        if (collaborators.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Collaborative document must have at least one collaborator");
        }
    }
    
    // Collaborative methods
    public void addCollaborator(String collaborator) {
        if (collaborator != null && !collaborator.trim().isEmpty() && 
            !collaborators.contains(collaborator.trim())) {
            collaborators.add(collaborator.trim());
            editHistory.put(collaborator.trim(), new Date());
        }
    }
    
    public void addComment(String comment) {
        if (comment != null && !comment.trim().isEmpty()) {
            comments.add(comment.trim());
        }
    }
    
    public boolean lockDocument(String user) {
        if (!isLocked && collaborators.contains(user)) {
            isLocked = true;
            lockOwner = user;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    public boolean unlockDocument(String user) {
        if (isLocked && user.equals(lockOwner)) {
            isLocked = false;
            lockOwner = null;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Getters
    public List<String> getCollaborators() { return new ArrayList<>(collaborators); }
    public Map<String, Date> getEditHistory() { 
        Map<String, Date> copy = new HashMap<>();
        for (Map.Entry<String, Date> entry : editHistory.entrySet()) {
            copy.put(entry.getKey(), 
                entry.getValue() != null ? new Date(entry.getValue().getTime()) : null);
        }
        return copy;
    }
    public boolean isLocked() { return isLocked; }
    public String getLockOwner() { return lockOwner; }
    public List<String> getComments() { return new ArrayList<>(comments); }
    
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return String.format("CollaborativeDocument{%s, collaborators=%d, locked=%s, comments=%d}", 
            super.toString(), collaborators.size(), isLocked, comments.size());
    }
}

/**
 * Copy constructor factory for handling complex copying scenarios
 */
public class DocumentCopyFactory {
    
    /**
     * Generic copy method using reflection and copy constructors
     */
    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    public static <T extends Document> T createCopy(T original) {
        if (original == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Original document cannot be null");
        }
        
        try {
            Class<T> clazz = (Class<T>) original.getClass();
            
            // Look for copy constructor
            Constructor<T> copyConstructor = clazz.getConstructor(clazz);
            return copyConstructor.newInstance(original);
            
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Failed to create copy of " + original.getClass().getSimpleName(), e);
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Deep copy with circular reference handling
     */
    public static Document createDeepCopy(Document original, Set<String> visitedIds) {
        if (original == null) {
            return null;
        }
        
        // Check for circular references
        if (visitedIds.contains(original.getDocumentId())) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Circular reference detected: " + original.getDocumentId());
        }
        
        visitedIds.add(original.getDocumentId());
        
        try {
            if (original instanceof TechnicalDocument) {
                return new TechnicalDocument((TechnicalDocument) original);
            } else if (original instanceof CollaborativeDocument) {
                return new CollaborativeDocument((CollaborativeDocument) original);
            } else {
                return new Document(original);
            }
        } finally {
            visitedIds.remove(original.getDocumentId());
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy with transformation
     */
    public static Document createTransformedCopy(Document original, 
                                               Function<Document, Document> transformer) {
        if (original == null || transformer == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Original document and transformer cannot be null");
        }
        
        Document copy = createCopy(original);
        return transformer.apply(copy);
    }
    
    /**
     * Batch copy operation
     */
    public static List<Document> createCopies(List<? extends Document> originals) {
        if (originals == null) {
            return new ArrayList<>();
        }
        
        return originals.stream()
                       .filter(Objects::nonNull)
                       .map(DocumentCopyFactory::createCopy)
                       .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }
}

/**
 * Copy constructor with validation and error handling
 */
public class ValidatedDocument extends Document {
    private final List<String> validationRules;
    private final Map<String, Object> validationCache;
    
    public ValidatedDocument(String documentId, String title, String author) {
        super(documentId, title, author);
        this.validationRules = new ArrayList<>();
        this.validationCache = new HashMap<>();
        addDefaultValidationRules();
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor with comprehensive validation
     */
    public ValidatedDocument(ValidatedDocument other) {
        super(other);
        
        if (other == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source validated document cannot be null");
        }
        
        // Deep copy validation data
        this.validationRules = other.validationRules != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(other.validationRules) : new ArrayList<>();
        this.validationCache = other.validationCache != null ? 
            new HashMap<>(other.validationCache) : new HashMap<>();
        
        // Validate the copied document
        validateDocument();
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor with validation override
     */
    public ValidatedDocument(Document baseDocument, List<String> customValidationRules) {
        super(baseDocument);
        
        this.validationRules = customValidationRules != null ? 
            new ArrayList<>(customValidationRules) : new ArrayList<>();
        this.validationCache = new HashMap<>();
        
        if (this.validationRules.isEmpty()) {
            addDefaultValidationRules();
        }
        
        validateDocument();
    }
    
    private void addDefaultValidationRules() {
        validationRules.add("TITLE_NOT_EMPTY");
        validationRules.add("AUTHOR_NOT_EMPTY");
        validationRules.add("CONTENT_LENGTH_VALID");
        validationRules.add("TAGS_FORMAT_VALID");
    }
    
    private void validateDocument() {
        for (String rule : validationRules) {
            switch (rule) {
                case "TITLE_NOT_EMPTY":
                    if (getTitle() == null || getTitle().trim().isEmpty()) {
                        throw new IllegalStateException("Document title cannot be empty");
                    }
                    break;
                case "AUTHOR_NOT_EMPTY":
                    if (getAuthor() == null || getAuthor().trim().isEmpty()) {
                        throw new IllegalStateException("Document author cannot be empty");
                    }
                    break;
                case "CONTENT_LENGTH_VALID":
                    if (getContent() != null && getContent().length() > 1_000_000) {
                        throw new IllegalStateException("Document content exceeds maximum length");
                    }
                    break;
                case "TAGS_FORMAT_VALID":
                    for (String tag : getTags()) {
                        if (tag.contains(" ") || tag.length() > 50) {
                            throw new IllegalStateException("Invalid tag format: " + tag);
                        }
                    }
                    break;
            }
        }
    }
    
    public List<String> getValidationRules() { 
        return new ArrayList<>(validationRules); 
    }
    
    public void addValidationRule(String rule) {
        if (rule != null && !validationRules.contains(rule)) {
            validationRules.add(rule);
            validateDocument(); // Re-validate with new rule
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Lazy copy constructor - defers expensive operations
 */
public class LazyDocument extends Document {
    private volatile String expensiveComputedField;
    private volatile boolean computedFieldInitialized = false;
    private final Object computationLock = new Object();
    
    public LazyDocument(String documentId, String title, String author) {
        super(documentId, title, author);
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor with lazy initialization preservation
     */
    public LazyDocument(LazyDocument other) {
        super(other);
        
        // Don't copy computed field - let it be computed lazily in the copy
        this.expensiveComputedField = null;
        this.computedFieldInitialized = false;
        // Note: computationLock is not copied - each instance has its own
    }
    
    /**
     * Expensive computation that should be done lazily
     */
    public String getExpensiveComputedField() {
        if (!computedFieldInitialized) {
            synchronized (computationLock) {
                if (!computedFieldInitialized) {
                    // Simulate expensive computation
                    expensiveComputedField = computeExpensiveField();
                    computedFieldInitialized = true;
                }
            }
        }
        return expensiveComputedField;
    }
    
    private String computeExpensiveField() {
        // Simulate expensive computation (e.g., content analysis, indexing)
        try {
            Thread.sleep(100); // Simulate computation time
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        }
        
        return "COMPUTED_" + getDocumentId() + "_" + System.currentTimeMillis();
    }
}

/**
 * Copy-on-write document for memory efficiency
 */
public class CopyOnWriteDocument extends Document {
    private volatile boolean isSharedState;
    private final Object modificationLock = new Object();
    
    public CopyOnWriteDocument(String documentId, String title, String author) {
        super(documentId, title, author);
        this.isSharedState = false;
    }
    
    /**
     * Copy constructor that shares state until modification
     */
    public CopyOnWriteDocument(CopyOnWriteDocument other) {
        super(other);
        this.isSharedState = true;
        other.isSharedState = true; // Mark original as shared too
    }
    
    /**
     * Override setters to implement copy-on-write
     */
    @Override
    public void setTitle(String title) {
        synchronized (modificationLock) {
            if (isSharedState) {
                // Create private copy before modification
                createPrivateCopy();
            }
            super.setTitle(title);
        }
    }
    
    @Override
    public void setContent(String content) {
        synchronized (modificationLock) {
            if (isSharedState) {
                createPrivateCopy();
            }
            super.setContent(content);
        }
    }
    
    private void createPrivateCopy() {
        // This would involve deep copying all mutable state
        // Implementation depends on specific requirements
        isSharedState = false;
    }
    
    public boolean isSharedState() {
        return isSharedState;
    }
}
```

### **Copy Constructor vs Other Patterns**

#### **Copy Constructor vs Clone Method**

```java
/**
 * Comparison of copy constructor vs Cloneable interface
 */
public class CloneableDocument extends Document implements Cloneable {
    
    public CloneableDocument(String documentId, String title, String author) {
        super(documentId, title, author);
    }
    
    // Copy constructor approach (RECOMMENDED)
    public CloneableDocument(CloneableDocument other) {
        super(other);
        // Type-safe, compile-time checked, clear semantics
    }
    
    // Clone method approach (PROBLEMATIC)
    @Override
    public CloneableDocument clone() {
        try {
            CloneableDocument cloned = (CloneableDocument) super.clone();
            // Must manually handle deep copying
            // Runtime exceptions possible
            // Less clear semantics
            return cloned;
        } catch (CloneNotSupportedException e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Clone not supported", e);
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Why Copy Constructors are preferred over clone():
 * 
 * 1. TYPE SAFETY: Copy constructors are type-safe at compile time
 * 2. NO EXCEPTIONS: No need to handle CloneNotSupportedException
 * 3. CLEAR SEMANTICS: Constructor syntax makes copying intent clear
 * 4. INHERITANCE FRIENDLY: Works naturally with inheritance hierarchies
 * 5. VALIDATION: Can include validation logic in constructor
 * 6. FLEXIBILITY: Can accept parameters for customized copying
 */
```

#### **Copy Constructor vs Builder Pattern**

```java
/**
 * Copy constructor integrated with Builder pattern
 */
public class DocumentBuilder {
    private Document baseDocument;
    private String newTitle;
    private String newContent;
    private List<String> additionalTags;
    
    // Start with existing document
    public static DocumentBuilder from(Document document) {
        DocumentBuilder builder = new DocumentBuilder();
        builder.baseDocument = document;
        return builder;
    }
    
    public DocumentBuilder withTitle(String title) {
        this.newTitle = title;
        return this;
    }
    
    public DocumentBuilder withContent(String content) {
        this.newContent = content;
        return this;
    }
    
    public DocumentBuilder addTag(String tag) {
        if (additionalTags == null) {
            additionalTags = new ArrayList<>();
        }
        additionalTags.add(tag);
        return this;
    }
    
    public Document build() {
        // Use copy constructor as foundation
        Document copy = new Document(baseDocument);
        
        // Apply modifications
        if (newTitle != null) {
            copy.setTitle(newTitle);
        }
        if (newContent != null) {
            copy.setContent(newContent);
        }
        if (additionalTags != null) {
            additionalTags.forEach(copy::addTag);
        }
        
        return copy;
    }
}
```

```java
/**
 * Comprehensive copy constructor implementation checklist
 */
public class CopyConstructorBestPractices {
    
    // ✅ ALWAYS do these:
    
    // 1. Null check the source object
    public Document(Document other) {
        if (other == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source document cannot be null");
        }
        // ... rest of implementation
    }
    
    // 2. Deep copy mutable objects
    this.tags = other.tags != null ? new ArrayList<>(other.tags) : new ArrayList<>();
    this.metadata = other.metadata != null ? new HashMap<>(other.metadata) : new HashMap<>();
    
    // 3. Handle Date objects properly (they're mutable!)
    this.createdDate = other.createdDate != null ? 
        new Date(other.createdDate.getTime()) : null;
    
    // 4. Validate the copied state
    private void validateCopiedState() {
        if (documentId == null || title == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Document copy is in invalid state");
        }
    }
    
    // 5. Call parent copy constructor in inheritance
    public TechnicalDocument(TechnicalDocument other) {
        super(other); // CRITICAL - call parent copy constructor first
        // ... copy derived fields
    }
    
    // ❌ NEVER do these:
    
    // 1. Don't shallow copy mutable objects
    // this.tags = other.tags; // WRONG - shared reference!
    
    // 2. Don't forget to copy derived class fields
    // public TechnicalDocument(TechnicalDocument other) {
    //     super(other);
    //     // Missing: this.technicalLevel = other.technicalLevel;
    // }
    
    // 3. Don't ignore null collections
    // this.tags = new ArrayList<>(other.tags); // NullPointerException if other.tags is null
    
    // 4. Don't copy locks or thread-specific state
    // this.lock = other.lock; // WRONG - each instance needs its own lock
}
```

### **Interview Follow-Up Questions**

1. **Q**: "Why doesn't Java have native copy constructors like C++?"
   **A**: Java design philosophy emphasizes:
   - **Explicit object creation**: `new` keyword makes object creation clear
   - **Garbage collection**: No need for copy semantics for memory management
   - **Reference semantics**: Objects are accessed via references, not values
   - **Alternative patterns**: Builder pattern, factory methods, clone() provide flexibility

2. **Q**: "How do you handle circular references in copy constructors?"
   **A**: Use visited object tracking:
   ```java
   public Document deepCopy(Set<String> visited) {
       if (visited.contains(this.documentId)) {
           throw new IllegalStateException("Circular reference detected");
       }
       visited.add(this.documentId);
       // Perform copy with visited set
   }
   ```

3. **Q**: "What's the performance impact of copy constructors vs other approaches?"
   **A**: 
   - **Copy constructor**: O(n) time, O(n) space for deep copying
   - **Shallow references**: O(1) time, O(1) space but shared mutable state
   - **Clone method**: Similar performance but with runtime overhead
   - **Immutable objects**: O(n) creation cost, then O(1) sharing

4. **Q**: "How do copy constructors work with generic types?"
   **A**: Use bounded wildcards and type safety:
   ```java
   public class GenericDocument<T> {
       public GenericDocument(GenericDocument<? extends T> other) {
           // Type-safe copying with generics
       }
   }
   ```

---

### **Complexity Analysis**

**Time Complexity**:
- **Simple copy constructor**: O(n) - Where n is number of fields to copy
- **Deep copy with collections**: O(m) - Where m is total elements in all collections
- **Inheritance hierarchy**: O(h × n) - Where h is inheritance depth

**Space Complexity**:
- **Deep copy**: O(n) - Creates new objects for all mutable references
- **Lazy copy**: O(1) - Defers expensive operations until needed
- **Copy-on-write**: O(1) initially, O(n) on first modification

**Performance Characteristics**:
- **Copy constructor**: 2-5x faster than clone() method
- **Validation overhead**: 10-20% additional time for validation
- **Memory efficiency**: Deep copy uses 2x memory during construction

---

This comprehensive analysis demonstrates that **copy constructors are the preferred pattern in Java** for safe object copying because they provide:

- **Type safety** at compile time without runtime exceptions
- **Clear semantics** that make copying intent obvious
- **Inheritance support** that works naturally with object hierarchies  
- **Validation opportunities** to ensure copied objects are in valid states
- **Performance benefits** over alternative approaches like clone()
- **Flexibility** to customize copying behavior based on requirements

The key insight is that **proper copy constructor implementation requires careful consideration of deep vs shallow copying, inheritance hierarchies, and validation**, making it a fundamental skill for enterprise Java development.

```java
/**
 * Comprehensive Object Class Demonstration System
 * 
 * This system demonstrates proper Object class method implementation
 * through a real-world enterprise employee management system where
 * proper equals(), hashCode(), and toString() are critical for
 * data integrity, performance, and debugging.

/**
 * Complete demonstration of all Object class methods
 */
public class ObjectMethodsDemo {
    
    public static void demonstrateObjectMethods() {
        System.out.println("=== OBJECT CLASS METHODS DEMONSTRATION ===\n");
        
        Employee emp1 = new Employee("EMP001", "John Doe", "Software Engineer", 75000);
        Employee emp2 = new Employee("EMP001", "John Doe", "Software Engineer", 75000);
        Employee emp3 = new Employee("EMP002", "Jane Smith", "Product Manager", 85000);
        
        // 1. toString() - String representation
        System.out.println("1. toString() method:");
        System.out.println("emp1.toString(): " + emp1.toString());
        System.out.println("emp1 (implicit): " + emp1); // Calls toString() automatically
        System.out.println();
        
        // 2. equals() - Logical equality
        System.out.println("2. equals() method:");
        System.out.println("emp1.equals(emp2): " + emp1.equals(emp2)); // Should be true
        System.out.println("emp1.equals(emp3): " + emp1.equals(emp3)); // Should be false
        System.out.println("emp1.equals(null): " + emp1.equals(null)); // Should be false
        System.out.println("emp1.equals(\"string\"): " + emp1.equals("string")); // Should be false
        System.out.println();
        
        // 3. hashCode() - Hash value for collections
        System.out.println("3. hashCode() method:");
        System.out.println("emp1.hashCode(): " + emp1.hashCode());
        System.out.println("emp2.hashCode(): " + emp2.hashCode()); // Should be same as emp1
        System.out.println("emp3.hashCode(): " + emp3.hashCode()); // Should be different
        System.out.println("Hash codes equal: " + (emp1.hashCode() == emp2.hashCode()));
        System.out.println();
        
        // 4. getClass() - Runtime type information
        System.out.println("4. getClass() method:");
        System.out.println("emp1.getClass(): " + emp1.getClass());
        System.out.println("emp1.getClass().getName(): " + emp1.getClass().getName());
        System.out.println("emp1.getClass().getSimpleName(): " + emp1.getClass().getSimpleName());
        System.out.println();
        
        // 5. clone() - Object copying (if implemented)
        System.out.println("5. clone() method:");
        try {
            Employee clonedEmp = emp1.clone();
            System.out.println("Original: " + emp1);
            System.out.println("Cloned: " + clonedEmp);
            System.out.println("Are they equal? " + emp1.equals(clonedEmp));
            System.out.println("Same reference? " + (emp1 == clonedEmp));
        } catch (CloneNotSupportedException e) {
            System.out.println("Clone not supported: " + e.getMessage());
        }
        System.out.println();
        
        // 6. finalize() - Cleanup before garbage collection (deprecated)
        System.out.println("6. finalize() method:");
        System.out.println("finalize() is deprecated since Java 9");
        System.out.println("Use try-with-resources or explicit cleanup methods instead");
        System.out.println();
        
        // 7. wait(), notify(), notifyAll() - Thread synchronization
        System.out.println("7. Synchronization methods:");
        System.out.println("wait(), notify(), notifyAll() are used for thread coordination");
        System.out.println("Must be called within synchronized blocks");
        System.out.println("See ThreadSafeEmployeeRegistry example below");
        System.out.println();
    }
}

/**
 * Employee class demonstrating proper Object method implementation
 */
public class Employee implements Cloneable {
    private final String employeeId;
    private String name;
    private String position;
    private double salary;
    private Date hireDate;
    private List<String> skills;
    private Address address;
    
    public Employee(String employeeId, String name, String position, double salary) {
        this.employeeId = validateEmployeeId(employeeId);
        this.name = validateName(name);
        this.position = validatePosition(position);
        this.salary = validateSalary(salary);
        this.hireDate = new Date();
        this.skills = new ArrayList<>();
        this.address = null;
    }
    
    /**
     * PROPER EQUALS() IMPLEMENTATION
     * 
     * Contract requirements:
     * 1. Reflexive: x.equals(x) must return true
     * 2. Symmetric: x.equals(y) == y.equals(x)
     * 3. Transitive: if x.equals(y) && y.equals(z), then x.equals(z)
     * 4. Consistent: multiple calls return same result
     * 5. Null handling: x.equals(null) must return false
     */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object obj) {
        // 1. Self-reference check (performance optimization)
        if (this == obj) {
            return true;
        }
        
        // 2. Null check (contract requirement)
        if (obj == null) {
            return false;
        }
        
        // 3. Type check (contract requirement)
        if (getClass() != obj.getClass()) {
            return false;
        }
        
        // 4. Cast and field comparison
        Employee other = (Employee) obj;
        
        // Use Objects.equals() for null-safe comparison
        return Objects.equals(employeeId, other.employeeId) &&
               Objects.equals(name, other.name) &&
               Objects.equals(position, other.position) &&
               Double.compare(salary, other.salary) == 0 &&
               Objects.equals(hireDate, other.hireDate) &&
               Objects.equals(skills, other.skills) &&
               Objects.equals(address, other.address);
    }
    
    /**
     * PROPER HASHCODE() IMPLEMENTATION
     * 
     * Contract requirements:
     * 1. If equals() returns true, hashCode() must return same value
     * 2. If equals() returns false, hashCode() should return different values (preferred)
     * 3. Multiple calls on same object must return same value
     * 4. Should distribute hash values evenly
     */
    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        // Use Objects.hash() for consistent hashing
        return Objects.hash(employeeId, name, position, salary, hireDate, skills, address);
    }
    
    /**
     * PROPER TOSTRING() IMPLEMENTATION
     * 
     * Best practices:
     * 1. Include class name
     * 2. Include key identifying fields
     * 3. Use consistent format
     * 4. Don't include sensitive information
     * 5. Keep it concise but informative
     */
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return String.format("Employee{id='%s', name='%s', position='%s', salary=%.2f, hireDate=%s}", 
            employeeId, name, position, salary, 
            hireDate != null ? hireDate.toString() : "null");
    }
    
    /**
     * PROPER CLONE() IMPLEMENTATION
     * 
     * Requirements:
     * 1. Implement Cloneable interface
     * 2. Handle CloneNotSupportedException
     * 3. Decide between shallow and deep copying
     * 4. Maintain object invariants
     */
    @Override
    public Employee clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        // Shallow clone first
        Employee cloned = (Employee) super.clone();
        
        // Deep clone mutable objects
        if (this.hireDate != null) {
            cloned.hireDate = new Date(this.hireDate.getTime());
        }
        
        if (this.skills != null) {
            cloned.skills = new ArrayList<>(this.skills);
        }
        
        if (this.address != null) {
            cloned.address = this.address.clone(); // Assuming Address implements clone()
        }
        
        return cloned;
    }
    
    /**
     * FINALIZE() - DEPRECATED SINCE JAVA 9
     * 
     * Problems with finalize():
     * 1. No guarantee when (or if) it will be called
     * 2. Performance impact on garbage collection
     * 3. Can cause memory leaks if objects are resurrected
     * 4. Better alternatives exist
     */
    @Deprecated
    @Override
    protected void finalize() throws Throwable {
        try {
            // Cleanup code (if any)
            System.out.println("Finalizing employee: " + employeeId);
        } finally {
            super.finalize();
        }
    }
    
    // Validation methods
    private String validateEmployeeId(String id) {
        if (id == null || id.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID cannot be null or empty");
        }
        return id.trim();
    }
    
    private String validateName(String name) {
        if (name == null || name.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee name cannot be null or empty");
        }
        return name.trim();
    }
    
    private String validatePosition(String position) {
        if (position == null || position.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee position cannot be null or empty");
        }
        return position.trim();
    }
    
    private double validateSalary(double salary) {
        if (salary < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Salary cannot be negative");
        }
        return salary;
    }
    
    // Getters and setters
    public String getEmployeeId() { return employeeId; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public String getPosition() { return position; }
    public double getSalary() { return salary; }
    public Date getHireDate() { return hireDate != null ? new Date(hireDate.getTime()) : null; }
    public List<String> getSkills() { return new ArrayList<>(skills); }
    public Address getAddress() { return address; }
    
    public void setName(String name) { this.name = validateName(name); }
    public void setPosition(String position) { this.position = validatePosition(position); }
    public void setSalary(double salary) { this.salary = validateSalary(salary); }
    public void setAddress(Address address) { this.address = address; }
    
    public void addSkill(String skill) {
        if (skill != null && !skill.trim().isEmpty()) {
            skills.add(skill.trim());
        }
    }
    
    public void removeSkill(String skill) {
        skills.remove(skill);
    }
}

/**
 * Address class for employee addresses

public class Address implements Cloneable {
    private String street;
    private String city;
    private String state;
    private String zipCode;
    private String country;
    
    public Address(String street, String city, String state, String zipCode, String country) {
        this.street = street;
        this.city = city;
        this.state = state;
        this.zipCode = zipCode;
        this.country = country;
    }
    
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object obj) {
        if (this == obj) return true;
        if (obj == null || getClass() != obj.getClass()) return false;
        
        Address address = (Address) obj;
        return Objects.equals(street, address.street) &&
               Objects.equals(city, address.city) &&
               Objects.equals(state, address.state) &&
               Objects.equals(zipCode, address.zipCode) &&
               Objects.equals(country, address.country);
    }
    
    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(street, city, state, zipCode, country);
    }
    
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return String.format("Address{street='%s', city='%s', state='%s', zip='%s', country='%s'}", 
            street, city, state, zipCode, country);
    }
    
    @Override
    public Address clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        return (Address) super.clone(); // Shallow clone is sufficient (all fields are immutable)
    }
    
    // Getters and setters
    public String getStreet() { return street; }
    public String getCity() { return city; }
    public String getState() { return state; }
    public String getZipCode() { return zipCode; }

    public void setStreet(String street) { this.street = street; }

    public void setZipCode(String zipCode) { this.zipCode = zipCode; }
    public void setCountry(String country) { this.country = country; }
}

// WAIT/NOTIFY SYNCHRONIZATION METHODS
// ============================================================================

/**
 * Thread-safe employee registry demonstrating wait/notify usage
 */
public class ThreadSafeEmployeeRegistry {
    private final Map<String, Employee> employees = new HashMap<>();
    private final Object lock = new Object();
    private volatile boolean dataReady = false;
    
    /**
     * Add employee with notification to waiting threads
     */
    public void addEmployee(Employee employee) {
        synchronized (lock) {
            employees.put(employee.getEmployeeId(), employee);
            dataReady = true;
            
            // Notify all waiting threads that data is available
            lock.notifyAll();
            
            System.out.println("Added employee: " + employee.getEmployeeId() + 
                             " (Total: " + employees.size() + ")");
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Wait for employee data to be available
     */
    public Employee waitForEmployee(String employeeId, long timeoutMs) throws InterruptedException {
        synchronized (lock) {
            long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
            
            while (!dataReady || !employees.containsKey(employeeId)) {
                long elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime;
                long remaining = timeoutMs - elapsed;
                
                if (remaining <= 0) {
                    throw new RuntimeException("Timeout waiting for employee: " + employeeId);
                }
                
                System.out.println("Waiting for employee: " + employeeId);
                lock.wait(remaining); // Wait with timeout
            }
            
            return employees.get(employeeId);
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Get employee count (thread-safe)
     */
    public int getEmployeeCount() {
        synchronized (lock) {
            return employees.size();
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Check if registry has data
     */
    public boolean hasData() {
        synchronized (lock) {
            return dataReady && !employees.isEmpty();
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Clear all data and notify waiting threads
     */
    public void clearData() {
        synchronized (lock) {
            employees.clear();
            dataReady = false;
            
            // Notify waiting threads that data has been cleared
            lock.notifyAll();
            
            System.out.println("Registry cleared");
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Demonstration of wait/notify in producer-consumer scenario
 */
public class EmployeeProcessingDemo {
    
    public static void demonstrateWaitNotify() throws InterruptedException {
        System.out.println("=== WAIT/NOTIFY DEMONSTRATION ===\n");
        
        ThreadSafeEmployeeRegistry registry = new ThreadSafeEmployeeRegistry();
        
        // Consumer thread - waits for employee data
        Thread consumer = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                System.out.println("Consumer: Waiting for employee EMP001...");
                Employee emp = registry.waitForEmployee("EMP001", 5000);
                System.out.println("Consumer: Received employee: " + emp);
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                System.out.println("Consumer interrupted");
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                System.out.println("Consumer: " + e.getMessage());
            }
        });
        
        // Producer thread - adds employee data
        Thread producer = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                Thread.sleep(2000); // Simulate processing delay
                
                Employee emp = new Employee("EMP001", "Alice Johnson", "Developer", 70000);
                System.out.println("Producer: Adding employee...");
                registry.addEmployee(emp);
                
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                System.out.println("Producer interrupted");
            }
        });
        
        // Start threads
        consumer.start();
        producer.start();
        
        // Wait for completion
        consumer.join();
        producer.join();
        
        System.out.println("Wait/notify demonstration completed\n");
    }
}

/**
 * Performance analysis of Object method implementations
 */
public class ObjectMethodPerformanceAnalysis {
    
    private static final int ITERATIONS = 1_000_000;
    
    public static void analyzePerformance() {
        System.out.println("=== OBJECT METHOD PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS ===\n");
        
        // Create test employees
        Employee emp1 = new Employee("EMP001", "John Doe", "Engineer", 75000);
        Employee emp2 = new Employee("EMP001", "John Doe", "Engineer", 75000);
        Employee emp3 = new Employee("EMP002", "Jane Smith", "Manager", 85000);
        
        // Benchmark equals() method
        benchmarkEquals(emp1, emp2, emp3);
        
        // Benchmark hashCode() method
        benchmarkHashCode(emp1, emp2, emp3);
        
        // Benchmark toString() method
        benchmarkToString(emp1);
        
        // Analyze hash distribution
        analyzeHashDistribution();
    }
    
    private static void benchmarkEquals(Employee emp1, Employee emp2, Employee emp3) {
        System.out.println("1. equals() Performance:");
        
        // Warm up JIT
        for (int i = 0; i < 100_000; i++) {
            emp1.equals(emp2);
            emp1.equals(emp3);
        }
        
        // Benchmark equal objects
        long startTime = System.nanoTime();
        for (int i = 0; i < ITERATIONS; i++) {
            emp1.equals(emp2); // Should be true
        }
        long equalTime = System.nanoTime() - startTime;
        
        // Benchmark unequal objects
        startTime = System.nanoTime();
        for (int i = 0; i < ITERATIONS; i++) {
            emp1.equals(emp3); // Should be false
        }
        long unequalTime = System.nanoTime() - startTime;
        
        System.out.printf("Equal objects: %.2f ns per call%n", (double) equalTime / ITERATIONS);
        System.out.printf("Unequal objects: %.2f ns per call%n", (double) unequalTime / ITERATIONS);
        System.out.println();
    }
    
    private static void benchmarkHashCode(Employee emp1, Employee emp2, Employee emp3) {
        System.out.println("2. hashCode() Performance:");
        
        // Warm up JIT
        for (int i = 0; i < 100_000; i++) {
            emp1.hashCode();
        }
        
        // Benchmark hashCode
        long startTime = System.nanoTime();
        for (int i = 0; i < ITERATIONS; i++) {
            emp1.hashCode();
        }
        long hashTime = System.nanoTime() - startTime;
        
        System.out.printf("hashCode(): %.2f ns per call%n", (double) hashTime / ITERATIONS);
        
        // Verify hash consistency
        int hash1 = emp1.hashCode();
        int hash2 = emp2.hashCode();
        int hash3 = emp3.hashCode();
        
        System.out.printf("Hash consistency: emp1=%d, emp2=%d, emp3=%d%n", hash1, hash2, hash3);
        System.out.printf("Equal objects same hash: %s%n", hash1 == hash2);
        System.out.println();
    }
    
    private static void benchmarkToString(Employee emp1) {
        System.out.println("3. toString() Performance:");
        
        // Warm up JIT
        for (int i = 0; i < 100_000; i++) {
            emp1.toString();
        }
        
        // Benchmark toString
        long startTime = System.nanoTime();
        for (int i = 0; i < ITERATIONS; i++) {
            emp1.toString();
        }
        long toStringTime = System.nanoTime() - startTime;
        
        System.out.printf("toString(): %.2f ns per call%n", (double) toStringTime / ITERATIONS);
        System.out.println("Sample output: " + emp1.toString());
        System.out.println();
    }
    
    private static void analyzeHashDistribution() {
        System.out.println("4. Hash Distribution Analysis:");
        
        Map<Integer, Integer> hashCounts = new HashMap<>();
        int totalEmployees = 10_000;
        
        // Generate employees with varying data
        for (int i = 0; i < totalEmployees; i++) {
            Employee emp = new Employee(
                "EMP" + String.format("%05d", i),
                "Employee " + i,
                "Position " + (i % 10),
                50000 + (i % 50000)
            );
            
            int hash = emp.hashCode();
            hashCounts.put(hash, hashCounts.getOrDefault(hash, 0) + 1);
        }
        
        // Analyze distribution
        int uniqueHashes = hashCounts.size();
        int collisions = totalEmployees - uniqueHashes;
        double collisionRate = (double) collisions / totalEmployees * 100;
        
        System.out.printf("Total employees: %d%n", totalEmployees);
        System.out.printf("Unique hash codes: %d%n", uniqueHashes);
        System.out.printf("Hash collisions: %d%n", collisions);
        System.out.printf("Collision rate: %.2f%%%n", collisionRate);
        
        // Find worst collision bucket
        int maxCollisions = hashCounts.values().stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).max().orElse(0);
        System.out.printf("Worst collision bucket: %d objects%n", maxCollisions);
        System.out.println();
    }
}

/**
 * Common mistakes and best practices for Object method implementation
 */
public class ObjectMethodBestPractices {
    
    /**
     * Common equals() implementation mistakes
     */
    public static class BadEqualsExample {
        private String name;
        private int age;
        
        // ❌ BAD: Violates equals() contract
        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object obj) {
            // Missing null check
            // Missing type check
            // Using == for String comparison
            BadEqualsExample other = (BadEqualsExample) obj;
            return name == other.name && age == other.age; // WRONG!
        }
        
        // ❌ BAD: No hashCode() override (violates contract)
        // If equals() is overridden, hashCode() must be too!
    }
    
    /**
     * Correct equals() implementation
     */
    public static class GoodEqualsExample {
        private String name;
        private int age;
        
        // ✅ GOOD: Proper equals() implementation
        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object obj) {
            if (this == obj) return true;                    // Self-reference
            if (obj == null) return false;                   // Null check
            if (getClass() != obj.getClass()) return false;  // Type check
            
            GoodEqualsExample other = (GoodEqualsExample) obj;
            return Objects.equals(name, other.name) &&       // Null-safe comparison
                   age == other.age;                         // Primitive comparison
        }
        
        // ✅ GOOD: Consistent hashCode() implementation
        @Override
        public int hashCode() {
            return Objects.hash(name, age);
        }
        
        // ✅ GOOD: Informative toString()
        @Override
        public String toString() {
            return String.format("GoodExample{name='%s', age=%d}", name, age);
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Performance considerations for equals() and hashCode()
     */
    public static class PerformanceOptimizedEmployee {
        private final String employeeId;  // Most discriminating field first
        private final String name;
        private final String department;
        private final double salary;
        
        // Cached hash code for performance (if object is immutable)
        private volatile int hashCode = 0;
        
        public PerformanceOptimizedEmployee(String employeeId, String name, String department, double salary) {
            this.employeeId = employeeId;
            this.name = name;
            this.department = department;
            this.salary = salary;
        }
        
        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object obj) {
            if (this == obj) return true;
            if (obj == null || getClass() != obj.getClass()) return false;
            
            PerformanceOptimizedEmployee other = (PerformanceOptimizedEmployee) obj;
            
            // Check most discriminating field first (employeeId is likely unique)
            return Objects.equals(employeeId, other.employeeId) &&
                   Objects.equals(name, other.name) &&
                   Objects.equals(department, other.department) &&
                   Double.compare(salary, other.salary) == 0;
        }
        
        @Override
        public int hashCode() {
            // Use cached hash code for immutable objects
            int result = hashCode;
            if (result == 0) {
                result = Objects.hash(employeeId, name, department, salary);
                hashCode = result;
            }
            return result;
        }
        
        @Override
        public String toString() {
            return String.format("Employee{id='%s', name='%s', dept='%s', salary=%.2f}", 
                employeeId, name, department, salary);
        }
    }
}
```
